/**
 * The presentation rules a renderer reads.
 *
 * Everything here exists to answer one complaint: "I don't know what belongs to
 * what, and I don't know what I'm looking at." The rules are about naming and
 * orientation, not decoration.
 */

/**
 * Text is never clipped mid-word.
 *
 * Measured on the shipped board: 7 of 10 subtitles were truncated, several by
 * 12-95px, on a viewport that was 85% empty. "the one test that isn't
 * implemented" — the most interesting claim on the screen — was cut at "isn'…".
 *
 * So: `blurb` wraps to at most BLURB_LINES lines and is never `truncate`d. If a
 * blurb does not fit in two lines it is too long and gets rewritten, not cut.
 */
export const BLURB_LINES = 2;

/**
 * Minimum readable width for the VALUE side of any two-column row.
 *
 * Measured failure: a `map` row was 212px wide, the label took 112px (53%), and
 * the value — the actual answer — got 32px, rendering one word per line over
 * twelve lines. The label is the question; the value is the answer; the answer
 * never gets less room than the question.
 */
export const ROW_LABEL_MAX_PCT = 40;
export const ROW_VALUE_MIN_PX = 160;

/**
 * Every card earns a SHAPE: something to recognise before reading anything.
 *
 * "Right now it's pretty boring to look at and it's pretty hard to understand
 * what's going on." A wall of uniform text gives the eye no purchase, so the
 * reader has to parse sentences to find out whether a card is even relevant.
 *
 * A shape is one of:
 *  - `marks`  brand glyphs for the real technologies involved (Bedrock, S3,
 *             Supabase, OpenAI). These are FACTS — every one is a dependency in
 *             the repo's package.json, not decoration.
 *  - `count`  a single number with a unit, where magnitude is the point.
 *
 * A card with nothing true to draw gets none. An invented diagram is the same
 * failure as an invented arrow (D19).
 */
export type Shape =
  | { kind: "marks"; ids: string[]; note?: string }
  | { kind: "count"; value: string; unit: string };

Claude Code, free in Blueprint

For a limited time, Blueprint pays for the Claude behind it. Making blueprints is unlimited, within fair use. Claude Code in Blueprint’s tabs gets about half of a Claude Pro plan.

What each person gets

What Allowance
Making blueprints Unlimited, within fair use: up to $200 of Claude a week per account, about sixteen blueprints of mid-size codebases. New blueprints and their updates both count. Past that, new blueprints run on your own Claude Code until the week resets.
Claude tabs, per session About half of a Claude Pro session, usually 15–40 prompts. The 5 hours start with your first message.
Claude tabs, per week About ten full sessions. The week starts with your first message.

It works like Claude Code’s own plans: a 5-hour session and a weekly limit. How many prompts fit depends on the work. Large codebases, long conversations and many files read in one turn use more. Claude tabs run Claude Sonnet, or Claude Haiku when Claude Code asks for it; a request for Opus runs on Sonnet. Settings → Blueprint credit shows how much of the session and the week you have used, and when each resets.

Who can use it

  • Anyone with Blueprint installed and a GitHub account at least 30 days old. Sign in with GitHub in Settings → Blueprint credit.
  • One allowance per GitHub account, on up to two computers.
  • You don’t need a Claude plan to use it.

How it may be used

  • Only inside Blueprint: its Claude tabs and its own blueprint generation. The credit doesn’t work outside the app.
  • Don’t share your sign-in, resell access, run automated workloads on it, or use more than one account to get more.
  • An account can run up to three Claude tab requests at once. Spending very fast slows requests down for a minute.
  • Accounts that misuse the credit can lose it without notice.

When it runs out

  • With Switch to my Claude Code when it runs out checked in Settings, which is the default, a Claude tab that hits its limit picks up the same conversation on your own Claude Code. You don’t have to sign in again. New tabs go back to Blueprint credit once it resets.
  • If you don’t have Claude Code signed in with a plan of your own, Claude tabs wait until the session or the week resets.
  • If the promotion’s budget for the whole month is used up, the credit pauses for everyone until the 1st of the next month.

When it ends

The promotion is for a limited time. Blueprint can change these allowances, or end the promotion, at any time. The end date is shown at the top of this page and in Settings. After it ends, Blueprint runs on your own Claude Code, as it does without the promotion.

Your data

Requests go from Blueprint to Blueprint’s server, which sends them to Claude on Amazon Bedrock. To enforce the limits, Blueprint keeps each request’s token counts, its cost and a coarse network for 30 days. It doesn’t keep what you or Claude wrote. Blueprints stay on your computer.
